project.name: unicorn
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable checkout reviewed here is the prepared Unicorn source under `gt_results/arvo_44659/_work/src/unicorn`; its line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer stack at `qemu/target/i386/ops_sse.h:2023`, `:2070`, and `:2112`. The staged `patch.diff` removes the hardcoded CPUID feature initialization from `qemu/target/i386/unicorn.c:x86_reg_reset`, including `CPUID_EXT_SSE42`, which is the feature bit that admits the crashing `pcmpestri` helper path in the reproduced trace.

classification.classification_note: The observed memory fault is a wild host read in `pcmp_val`, but the enabling root cause is the incorrect CPUID feature state seeded by `x86_reg_reset`. The first admitted `pcmpestri` helper call runs with zeroed length registers and only seeds `ECX`; later guest arithmetic and the backward `loop` make `EAX`/`EDX` nonzero, and the second admitted `pcmpestri` iteration reaches the sink.

bug_description.original: The vulnerability is that cpuid results are hardcoded in the code, rather than being set by the selected CPU. This can lead to incorrect or insecure behavior if the cpuid values do not match the actual CPU configuration.
bug_description.original_source: CyberGym tasks.json / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 18-byte raw x86-32 guest-code blob `c4 e3 f1 61 f1 29 00 c6 2d 00 00 00 66 2b d0 ee e2 ee` with sha256 `ad54fc539586be957843f98b13278af7210aaced472b47b23d8ed5e8c10cb535`. `fuzz_emu_x86_32` opens a fresh `UC_ARCH_X86` / `UC_MODE_32` engine, and the first later `uc_mem_map()` call enters lazy `UC_INIT(uc)` while `init_done` is still false. Inside that path, `uc_init()` reaches vulnerable `x86_reg_reset()`, which hardcodes `env->features[FEAT_1_ECX]` to include `CPUID_EXT_SSE42` and also zeroes `env->regs`. After the harness writes the witness bytes at guest address `0x1000000` and starts emulation, translation snapshots that reset feature mask into `dc->cpuid_ext_features`. In `gen_sse()`, opcode byte `0x61` selects the `pcmpestri` entry from `sse_op_table7`, the guard at `translate.c:4409` stays false because SSE4.2 is advertised, and lines 4568-4581 read the guest control byte `0x29`, materialize the operand pointers, and dispatch the helper. On the first helper invocation, zeroed EAX and EDX make both `pcmp_elen()` calls return 0, so `pcmpxstrx()` case 2 does not execute its `pcmp_val()` loop; instead `helper_pcmpestri_xmm_x86_64` leaves `res = 0xff` and writes `ECX = 0`. The remaining guest bytes then execute `sub eax, 0x66000000`, `sub edx, eax`, and `loop -18`, which change EAX to `0x9a000000`, EDX to `0x66000000`, decrement ECX to `0xffffffff`, and branch back to offset 0. On that later iteration the same admitted `pcmpestri` helper sees both length registers clamp to 8, `pcmpxstrx()` enters its case-2 per-element loop, and the saved stack line `ops_sse.h:2070` calls `pcmp_val(s, ctrl, i)`, whose 16-bit `r->W(i)` dereference faults at `qemu/target/i386/ops_sse.h:2023`, matching the saved AddressSanitizer `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` trace. The staged patch removes the hardcoded CPUID feature initialization from `x86_reg_reset`, including `CPUID_EXT_SSE42`, which source-levelly closes this admission path. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

source.description: First non-harness project statement on the admitted helper path that consumes the attacker-controlled guest byte stream into vulnerability-relevant decode state. The immediate-SSE decoder uses the guest opcode byte to select the helper slot, and for the staged witness this lookup resolves to the `pcmpestri` entry.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 18-byte blob `c4 e3 f1 61 f1 29 00 c6 2d 00 00 00 66 2b d0 ee e2 ee` (sha256 `ad54fc539586be957843f98b13278af7210aaced472b47b23d8ed5e8c10cb535`). When Unicorn decodes the `0f 3a` immediate-SSE map for this witness, the opcode byte consumed into `b` is `0x61`, which `sse_op_table7` maps to `pcmpestri`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The exact witness bytes are copied verbatim into the emulator's guest memory at `ADDRESS`, becoming the instruction stream later fetched by the x86 decoder and later re-fetched by the backward guest `loop`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged `poc` is 18 bytes long and contains exactly `c4 e3 f1 61 f1 29 00 c6 2d 00 00 00 66 2b d0 ee e2 ee`; those bytes are written unchanged into guest memory before `uc_emu_start()` begins decoding.

root_cause.code: env->features[FEAT_1_ECX] = CPUID_EXT_SSSE3 | CPUID_EXT_SSE41 | CPUID_EXT_SSE42 | CPUID_EXT_AES | CPUID_EXT_CX16;
root_cause.description: Root cause. Every fresh x86 engine reset unconditionally seeds the extended CPUID feature mask with `CPUID_EXT_SSE42` instead of leaving feature exposure to the selected CPU configuration. Later decode trusts that stale bit and admits the guest's `pcmpestri` instruction.
root_cause.note: On the reproduced path this assignment executes under the lazy `UC_INIT` entered by the first `uc_mem_map()` call. The staged patch removes this hardcoded feature initialization block, including `CPUID_EXT_SSE42`, so the vulnerable build no longer advertises SSE4.2 here.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer-observed crash site. On the second guest iteration, `pcmpxstrx` line 2070 calls `pcmp_val(s, ctrl, i)`, and this line dereferences that operand pointer as a 16-bit lane array, producing the recorded wild-address read.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: SEGV (wild-addr-read)` at `qemu/target/i386/ops_sse.h:2023:16` in `pcmp_val`, with the stack `pcmp_val -> pcmpxstrx -> helper_pcmpestri_xmm_x86_64` and frame 1 at `ops_sse.h:2070`.

parser_admitted.description: There is no container or file parser in this sample: after the raw witness bytes have been written into guest memory, this call hands control to Unicorn's x86 decoder and starts fetching them as instructions from `ADDRESS`.

fine_trace.note: The harness creates a fresh x86-32 Unicorn engine handle for this input. In this tree `uc_open()` only allocates and configures that handle; it does not run `x86_reg_reset()`, so the new handle still has `init_done == false` when the next API call arrives.

The first library API on that fresh handle is `uc_mem_map()`, which executes `UC_INIT(uc)`. The macro's `!(uc)->init_done` guard is true here, so it enters `uc_init()`, runs `machine_initialize(uc)`, and then reaches `uc->reg_reset(uc)` on this lazy-init path.

fine_trace.code: env->features[FEAT_1_ECX] = CPUID_EXT_SSSE3 | CPUID_EXT_SSE41 | CPUID_EXT_SSE42 | CPUID_EXT_AES | CPUID_EXT_CX16;
fine_trace.note: Root cause. Within the lazy init entered in step 2, `uc->reg_reset(uc)` reaches `x86_reg_reset()` and unconditionally advertises SSE4.2 in the CPU extended feature mask for every x86 engine instance. The staged patch removes this hardcoded CPUID seeding, so later decode no longer inherits `CPUID_EXT_SSE42` from reset.

The same reset call zeroes the general-purpose register array, including EAX, ECX, and EDX. Those zero values become the first `pcmpestri` iteration's length inputs and explain why the initial helper entry does not yet reach `pcmp_val`.

The exact 18 attacker-controlled bytes are copied verbatim into guest memory at `ADDRESS = 0x1000000`. This mapped region becomes the instruction stream later fetched by the x86 decoder and later re-fetched by the witness's backward `loop`.

When `uc_emu_start()` begins translating the guest bytes, decode snapshots the reset CPUID extended-feature mask into `dc->cpuid_ext_features`. Because of step 3, this local decoder state still carries `CPUID_EXT_SSE42`.

Source. In the `0f 3a` immediate-SSE decoder, the guest opcode byte from the exact witness indexes `sse_op_table7`. For this witness, opcode `0x61` selects the `pcmpestri` helper slot, turning the attacker-controlled guest bytes into the specific helper dispatch used on both iterations of the crashing path.

For the `pcmpestri` table entry selected in step 7, `sse_op_table7[b].ext_mask` is `CPUID_EXT_SSE42`. Because step 6 preserved that hardcoded bit, this illegal-instruction guard is false and translation continues into the helper path instead of rejecting the opcode.

fine_trace.code: sse_fn_eppi(tcg_ctx, tcg_ctx->cpu_env, s->ptr0, s->ptr1, tcg_const_i32(tcg_ctx, val));
fine_trace.note: After the guard in step 8 is not taken, translation reads the instruction's immediate byte at line 4568 and dispatches the helper at line 4581. For the staged witness, `val` is `0x29`, whose low bits later make `pcmp_val()` choose 16-bit lanes and whose bits 3:2 later select `pcmpxstrx()` case 2. The same translated helper call is re-entered after the guest `loop` branches back to offset 0.

fine_trace.code: unsigned int res = pcmpxstrx(env, d, s, ctrl, pcmp_elen(env, R_EDX, ctrl), pcmp_elen(env, R_EAX, ctrl));
fine_trace.note: On the first execution of the helper dispatched in step 9, the zeroed EDX and EAX from step 4 make both `pcmp_elen()` calls return 0. After `pcmpxstrx()` decrements those counts to `-1`, case 2 at lines 2065-2072 does not iterate, so this first helper entry does not yet call `pcmp_val`.
Because the zero-length case-2 path in step 10 leaves `res = 0xff`, the helper takes the `if (res)` branch and stores `ECX = 0`. That register value later drives the witness's backward `loop`.

Bytes at witness offsets 8..12 execute this subtraction after the first helper returns, changing EAX from 0 to `0x9a000000` (`-1711276032`). The earlier offset-6 instruction `add dh, al` leaves DH unchanged because AL and DH are both 0 after step 4, so it contributes no new vulnerability-relevant state.

This next guest subtraction uses the updated EAX from step 12 to change EDX from 0 to `0x66000000` (`1711276032`). The intervening offset-15 instruction `out dx, al` does not modify EAX, EDX, or ECX, so it is omitted as non-contributing.

The final two witness bytes `e2 ee` decrement ECX from step 11's value 0 to `0xffffffff`; because the result is nonzero, control jumps back 18 bytes to offset 0 and re-executes the same 6-byte `pcmpestri` instruction with the updated EAX and EDX from steps 12 and 13.

fine_trace.code: unsigned int res = pcmpxstrx(env, d, s, ctrl, pcmp_elen(env, R_EDX, ctrl), pcmp_elen(env, R_EAX, ctrl));
fine_trace.note: On the re-entered `pcmpestri` from step 14, the helper sees the same `ctrl = 0x29` and operand pointers from step 9, but now `pcmp_elen(env, R_EDX, ctrl)` and `pcmp_elen(env, R_EAX, ctrl)` both clamp to 8 because steps 12 and 13 made `abs1((int32_t)EDX)` and `abs1((int32_t)EAX)` far larger than 8.

fine_trace.var: valids, validd, i, ctrl, s, d
fine_trace.note: With both helper lengths now 8, `pcmpxstrx()` decrements them to 7 and enters case 2. The loop runs for `i = 7..0`, and line 2070 calls `pcmp_val(s, ctrl, i)` before line 2071 compares it against `pcmp_val(d, ctrl, i)`.

depends_on.via: pcmp_elen(env, R_EDX, ctrl), pcmp_elen(env, R_EAX, ctrl)

fine_trace.note: Sink. The saved frame-1 call site at step 16 passes the `s` operand pointer into `pcmp_val`. Because `ctrl = 0x29` makes `((ctrl >> 0) & 3) == 1`, `pcmp_val()` takes the 16-bit case and dereferences `r->W(i)`, which AddressSanitizer records as the wild read at `0x62e100014ea6`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch removes the hardcoded CPUID feature initialization from `x86_reg_reset`, including `CPUID_EXT_SSE42`. Without that bit, the guard at `translate.c:4409` rejects opcode `0x61` instead of admitting either `pcmpestri` iteration, so the later guest arithmetic and backward `loop` no longer lead back into the crashing helper path. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image.

poc.trigger: The staged 18-byte witness `poc` (sha256 `ad54fc539586be957843f98b13278af7210aaced472b47b23d8ed5e8c10cb535`) reproduces the saved `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` in `pcmp_val` when `fuzz_emu_x86_32` executes it as raw guest code.

format.name: 18-byte raw x86-32 guest-code loop with a backward branch
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 18-byte witness `c4 e3 f1 61 f1 29 00 c6 2d 00 00 00 66 2b d0 ee e2 ee` (sha256 `ad54fc539586be957843f98b13278af7210aaced472b47b23d8ed5e8c10cb535`) executed by `fuzz_emu_x86_32` at `ADDRESS = 0x1000000`. The first 6 bytes must still reach Unicorn's admitted `pcmpestri` helper path with control byte `0x29`; the following guest bytes must still preserve the arithmetic `sub eax, 0x66000000` and `sub edx, eax`; and the final `loop -18` must still branch back to offset 0 after the first helper stores `ECX = 0`. Under those exact witnessed conditions, the second `pcmpestri` iteration reaches `pcmpxstrx` case 2 and the saved `pcmp_val` 16-bit read. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader trigger class than witnesses preserving this same helper admission, register-mutation, and backward-branch sequence under the vulnerable hardcoded `CPUID_EXT_SSE42` exposure.
